text:
Forensic findings CASEID
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office receives documents through intake channels, assigns each item a unique identifier, and stores it in designated filing systems. Records carry metadata fields such as creation date, author, case-type designation, and retention class. Access is logged by account, and periodic audits reconcile stored documents against access logs. Communication channels used for record-related correspondence are documented, and any channel that lacks standard audit logging is flagged for review. The office retains records per schedule, archives superseded versions, and maintains a chain of custody for anything designated as evidentiary. No intake-specific facts belong in this section; it describes only the filing, retention, and audit mechanics common to such offices.

2) What occurred: The actor prepared a coordination document referencing multiple property-management accounts, each identified by a named account field. The document contained a neighborhood-division table with a district assignment field per account and a rent-leveling schedule with a target-price field and an effective-date field. A compliance clause appeared in a penalty-field section specifying consequences for an underpricing entry detected in a competitor's public listing. The actor opened a side-channel account on an intermediary messaging platform, designated in the records as a non-standard channel, and exchanged dated records with counterparts through it. Each exchanged record carried a version number and a timestamp field. A routing field in the documents referenced the intermediary channel by identifier rather than a standard internal channel.

3) Materials/access observed: A coordination document in a shared drive folder named with a project-code value; the folder's access list contained four named accounts, one of which belonged to an external property-management firm. A spreadsheet with columns for district, baseline price, target price, and effective date. The side-channel account on the intermediary platform, created on a dated record, with message history exported as a dated file. Access logs showed the actor's account reading the shared drive folder at a timestamp field consistent with the effective-date field in the document.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A case-type field value inconsistent with the document's content in the filing system. A named account appearing in both the shared drive access list and the intermediary channel membership. A penalty clause field using conditional language tied to a detected underpricing value. A routing field pointing to a channel identifier absent from the standard channel registry. A message export file with timestamps aligning to within minutes of the effective-date field in the rent schedule. A version history showing the penalty-field section was added in a later revision by a second named account.
